A gene set is a named list of genes that share a pathway or function, such as "oxidative
phosphorylation". Set-level methods ask whether a set's proteins move together. This step decides
set membership once, for every set-level analysis: which protein stands for each gene, which sets
are tested, and which genes each set holds in this experiment.

## Packages

GSEABase reads the GO Slim file and GO.db supplies the Gene Ontology hierarchy; both are called
with `::` where used.

```{r}
#| label: packages
#| message: false
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
source(here("00_Setup", "Shared_functions", "workbooks.R"))
inputs <- c(
  proteins = "01_Processing/02_Quantification/c_data/quantification.rds",
  msigdb = "01_Processing/04_Gene_Sets/references/msigdb_2026.1.Hs.rds",
  goslim = "01_Processing/04_Gene_Sets/references/goslim_generic.obo"
)
paths <- vapply(inputs, here, character(1))
stopifnot(file.exists(paths))
```

## Inputs

The protein list and its annotation come from limpa's protein `EList` (`genes`: gene symbol,
precursor count `NPrec`, share of precursor values observed `PropObs`). Membership never reads a
protein value or a fold change. Two fixed snapshots sit in `references/` (sources in
`references/README.md`):

- MSigDB release 2026.1.Hs, saved from msigdbr. It supplies Hallmark, Reactome, KEGG Legacy and GO
  Biological Process (GO:BP) membership. Membership shifts between releases, so the release is read
  from the snapshot, not from the installed package.
- The GO Consortium's generic GO Slim, a short list of broad GO terms.

```{r}
#| label: inputs
proteins <- readRDS(paths[["proteins"]])
msigdb <- readRDS(paths[["msigdb"]])
collections <- msigdb$collections
membership <- rename(msigdb$membership, collection = database)
msigdb$db_version
count(distinct(membership, set_id, collection), collection)
```

## One protein per gene

Set methods need one row per gene symbol. The symbol is the first in `Genes` when limpa lists
several; a protein with none is dropped. When two proteins share a symbol, the one with the higher
share of observed precursor values (`PropObs`) represents it, then the one with more precursors
(`NPrec`), then the lower accession. The rule reads detection only.

```{r}
#| label: protein-map
protein_map <- proteins$genes |>
  as_tibble(rownames = "uniprot_id") |>
  transmute(
    uniprot_id,
    gene = trimws(sub(";.*", "", Genes)),
    n_precursors = NPrec,
    prop_observed = PropObs,
    mapping_status = if_else(is.na(gene) | !nzchar(gene), "missing_symbol", "candidate"),
    gene = if_else(mapping_status == "candidate", gene, NA_character_)
  )
representatives <- protein_map |>
  filter(mapping_status == "candidate") |>
  arrange(gene, desc(prop_observed), desc(n_precursors), uniprot_id) |>
  distinct(gene, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  pull(uniprot_id)
c(proteins = nrow(protein_map), representatives = length(representatives))
```

Plot labels must be unique, so a symbol shared by two proteins gets its accession appended.

```{r}
#| label: labels
protein_map <- protein_map |>
  mutate(
    selected = uniprot_id %in% representatives,
    mapping_status = case_when(
      selected ~ "representative",
      mapping_status == "candidate" ~ "duplicate_gene",
      .default = mapping_status
    ),
    label = if_else(
      is.na(gene), uniprot_id,
      if_else(duplicated(gene) | duplicated(gene, fromLast = TRUE),
        paste0(gene, " (", uniprot_id, ")"), gene
      )
    )
  )
gene_universe <- protein_map$gene[protein_map$selected]
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(protein_map$label))
mapping_summary <- count(protein_map, mapping_status, name = "n_proteins")
mapping_summary
filter(protein_map, gene %in% gene[mapping_status == "duplicate_gene"])
```

One symbol, MOCS2, is carried by two proteins (MOCS2A and MOCS2B); the one with the higher
observed share stands for it. The gene universe, the genes this experiment can speak to, holds
`r length(gene_universe)` genes.

## Which MSigDB sets qualify by size

Each set is cut down to the genes measured here. A set qualifies by size when its source size is 15
to 500 genes and at least 15 of them were measured. 15 to 500 is the GSEA software's default range,
and the manuscript uses the same bounds.

```{r}
#| label: msigdb-sets
set_members <- distinct(membership, set_id, gene)
sets_full <- split(set_members$gene, set_members$set_id)
sets_measured <- map(sets_full, intersect, y = gene_universe)
set_catalog <- membership |>
  distinct(set_id, collection, pathway, source_id, description) |>
  mutate(
    source_size = lengths(sets_full)[set_id],
    measured_size = lengths(sets_measured)[set_id],
    size_ok = source_size >= 15 & source_size <= 500 & measured_size >= 15
  )
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(set_catalog$set_id))
count(set_catalog, collection, size_ok)
```

## GO Slim sets

GO terms form a hierarchy, and a broad term covers every narrower term beneath it. Each GO Slim
term becomes a set holding every measured gene annotated to it or to any term below it. The genes
come from the full MSigDB GO:BP membership, so a gene is not lost when its own GO:BP set failed the
size rule. A slim term is broad by design, so the 15-to-500 rule reads measured size only. GO Slim
is an overview family: its sets nest and overlap the GO:BP sets.

```{r}
#| label: go-slim
slim_offspring <- AnnotationDbi::mget(
  GSEABase::ids(GSEABase::getOBOCollection(paths[["goslim"]])), GO.db::GOBPOFFSPRING,
  ifnotfound = NA
)
slim_offspring <- slim_offspring[!is.na(slim_offspring)]
go_genes <- membership |>
  filter(collection == "GOBP") |>
  with(split(gene, source_id))
slim_sets <- imap(slim_offspring, function(descendants, slim_id) {
  covered <- intersect(c(slim_id, descendants), names(go_genes))
  sort(intersect(unique(unlist(go_genes[covered], use.names = FALSE)), gene_universe))
})
slim_catalog <- tibble(
  theme_id = names(slim_sets),
  pathway = unname(AnnotationDbi::Term(GO.db::GOTERM[theme_id])),
  measured_size = lengths(slim_sets)
) |>
  transmute(
    set_id = paste("GO_Slim", toupper(gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", pathway)), sep = "|"),
    collection = "GO_Slim", pathway, source_id = theme_id,
    description = "GO Slim term: every measured gene under it in the GO:BP hierarchy",
    source_size = NA_integer_, measured_size,
    size_ok = measured_size >= 15 & measured_size <= 500
  )
names(slim_sets) <- slim_catalog$set_id
set_catalog <- bind_rows(set_catalog, slim_catalog)
sets_measured <- c(sets_measured, slim_sets)
c(slim_terms = nrow(slim_catalog), slim_size_ok = sum(slim_catalog$size_ok))
```

## Disease sets are left out

KEGG, Reactome and GO include sets named for a disease or a pathogen ("KEGG_PARKINSONS_DISEASE",
"REACTOME_SARS_COV_2_INFECTION"). In healthy muscle they mostly repackage mitochondrial, ribosomal
or signalling proteins already covered by the process sets, and a hit reads as a disease claim the
study cannot make. They are removed by name, not by content: a set is a disease set when a whole
word of its name (underscores split words, a trailing S allowed) is one of `disease_words`. The one
name that matches but is not a disease, the cytokine leukaemia inhibitory factor, is listed in
`not_disease` and kept. The rule runs on every collection; Hallmark names match none of the words.

```{r}
#| label: disease-rule
disease_words <- c(
  "DISEASE", "DISORDER", "INFECTION", "CANCER", "CARCINOMA", "ONCOGENIC", "LEUKEMIA", "LYMPHOMA",
  "GLIOMA", "MELANOMA", "SARCOMA", "DIABETES", "CARDIOMYOPATHY", "MYOCARDITIS", "SCLEROSIS",
  "LUPUS", "ASTHMA", "ARTHRITIS", "VIRAL", "VIRUS", "SYMBIONT", "INFLUENZA", "DENGUE", "HIV",
  "HCMV", "SARS", "MEASLES", "HERPES", "HEPATITIS", "TUBERCULOSIS", "MALARIA", "LEISHMANIA",
  "TOXOPLASMOSIS", "SALMONELLA", "SHIGELLOSIS", "HUNTINGTON", "PARKINSON", "ALZHEIMER", "PRION"
)
not_disease <- "LEUKEMIA_INHIBITORY_FACTOR"
disease_rule <- paste0("(^|_)(", paste(disease_words, collapse = "|"), ")S?(_|$)")
set_catalog <- set_catalog |>
  mutate(
    name_key = toupper(gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", pathway)),
    disease_set = grepl(disease_rule, name_key) & !grepl(not_disease, name_key),
    qualifies = size_ok & !disease_set
  ) |>
  select(-name_key)
disease_excluded <- set_catalog |>
  filter(size_ok, disease_set) |>
  select(set_id, collection, pathway, source_size, measured_size)
count(disease_excluded, collection)
print(select(disease_excluded, collection, pathway), n = Inf)
```

The rule removes host-defence and host-machinery sets as well ("response to virus", "viral gene
expression", "viral process", "symbiont entry into host"), because their names carry "virus",
"viral" or "symbiont". They are listed above and in the `disease_excluded` sheet;
add a name to `not_disease` to bring one back.

```{r}
#| label: tested-sets
sets <- sets_measured[set_catalog$set_id[set_catalog$qualifies]]
c(tested = length(sets), excluded_disease = nrow(disease_excluded))
```

## Validation

Every set name is unique, every tested set meets its size rule and is not a disease set, and every
member is in the gene universe.

```{r}
#| label: validate
stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(set_catalog$set_id), !anyDuplicated(names(sets)),
  all(lengths(sets) >= 15), all(lengths(sets) <= 500),
  all(unlist(sets) %in% gene_universe),
  !any(names(sets) %in% disease_excluded$set_id),
  setequal(names(sets), set_catalog$set_id[set_catalog$qualifies])
)
```

## Summary

```{r}
#| label: summary
collection_summary <- set_catalog |>
  summarise(
    n_in_source = n(), n_size_ok = sum(size_ok), n_disease = sum(size_ok & disease_set),
    n_qualifying = sum(qualifies), median_measured = median(measured_size[qualifies]),
    .by = collection
  ) |>
  arrange(match(collection, c(collections, "GO_Slim")))
collection_summary
```

`r nrow(protein_map)` proteins map to `r length(gene_universe)` genes. `r length(sets)` sets
qualify across `r nrow(collection_summary)` collections, after `r nrow(disease_excluded)` disease
sets were removed by name.

## Save

`gene_sets.rds` holds the tested sets, the full catalogue (with `size_ok`, `disease_set` and
`qualifies`), the protein-to-gene map and the gene universe; every set-level step reads it.

```{r}
#| label: save
out <- here("01_Processing", "04_Gene_Sets", "c_data")
dir.create(out, showWarnings = FALSE)
saveRDS(
  list(
    sets = sets, set_catalog = set_catalog, protein_map = protein_map,
    gene_universe = gene_universe
  ),
  file.path(out, "gene_sets.rds"),
  compress = "xz"
)
sheets <- list(
  collection_summary = collection_summary,
  disease_excluded = disease_excluded,
  set_catalog = set_catalog,
  protein_gene_map = protein_map,
  mapping_summary = mapping_summary
)
holds <- c(
  "Sets per collection: in the source, passing the size rule, removed as disease, tested.",
  "Sets that pass the size rule but are removed because their name matches the disease rule.",
  "Every set with its source and measured size, the size rule, the disease flag, and qualifies.",
  "Every protein, its gene symbol, and the representative chosen per symbol.",
  "Proteins per mapping status."
)
write_workbook(sheets, holds, file.path(out, "gene_sets.xlsx"), inputs, paths)
```
